rachel: Heads-up: TrustBank wants a tight POC next week. Requirements: streaming demo, strict JSON schema enforcement before any CRM call, and a pattern so their CRM only ever sees customer IPs. They also asked for reserved-pilot pricing and SOC2/SSO docs.

omar: We can do a small streaming UI + final validated JSON. For CRM privacy: recommend a customer-run connector in their VPC that proxies requests; for demo we can show a local proxy. If they need Redwood static IPs, that pushes to Dedicated/Private.

dean: KMS note: Hosted POC -> mock KMS/envelope encryption. Dedicated -> cloud KMS integration. Private -> customer-managed keys or HSM option (longer lead). I'll summarize differences for the call.

rachel: Two specific asks from TrustBank: 1) Can runtime reject malformed JSON (and not forward to CRM)? 2) Can tool calls be retried or audited when schema validation fails?

omar: Yes. We have runtime schema validation hooks. Behavior options: block + return validation error, auto-retry with constrained prompt (up to N attempts), or fallback to human review queue. All events get logged to audit. We'll demo block + one auto-retry.

dean: Pricing: for a short POC we offer hosted credits. For reserved pilot we can propose a 1-month small GPU pool (quote + overage). Send expected qps and avg tokens and Sarah on pricing will model it.

sales-bot: Quick python example to copy into the repo:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED")

# stream tokens to UI
for chunk in client.generate_stream(model="rwd-medium-1", prompt="Lookup customer 900 and respond with JSON:"):
    print(chunk.text, end="")

# final call with runtime schema validation enabled
resp = client.generate(
    model="rwd-medium-1",
    prompt="Produce JSON matching schema: {\"customer_id\":int,\"risk\":string}",
    output_schema='{"type":"object","properties":{"customer_id":{"type":"integer"},"risk":{"type":"string"}},"required":["customer_id","risk"]}',
    validate_schema=True,
    schema_retry=1
)
if resp.valid:
    # forward to customer connector (runs in their VPC)
    forward_to_connector(resp.json)
else:
    print('validation failed:', resp.errors)
```
